To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the blood-brain barrier to zinc in the rat is low and that the blood-brains exchange of zinc occurs mainly at the choroid plemxuses.

the blood-brain and blood-cerebro-spinal fluid barrier permeabilities to zinc are very low, and that the blood-cerebro-cerebro-spino fluid route accounts for less than 5% of total Zn influx to the brain.
the blood-brain barrier is relatively impermeable to Zn, that the blood-csf barrier to Zn is more permeable and that Zn accumulates in the brain in regions associated with neuronal activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transport of65Zn into the brain, its distribution and its possible role in the pathophysiology of neurodegeneration.
the mechanisms by which the CNS regulates its zinc levels and the role of zinc in the development and function of neurons and glia.
the role of zinc in the central nervous system, in particular, the role of the metal in brain development, function and neurodegeneration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the choroid plesxus is the main site of Zn influx into the CNS, and that this is a slow process, but the major route of Zn entry into the CNS is via the blood-brain barrier, a process that is very rapid.
the blood-brain exchange routes for65Zn are cerebral capillaries and the choroid plesuxes.
the choroid plevxus is a major site of Zn influx into the brain and Zn is distributed in a non-uniform manner in brain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the brain is a net exporter of65Zn to blood.
the brain is relatively impermeable to65Zn, but that the choroid pplexus may be important for the regulation of brain Zn homeostatis.
the blood-cerebro-spinal fluid barrier is not the primary route for the movement of Zn from blood to brain and that the brain capillaries are the main entry site for Zn.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the blood brain barrier to Zn is very low and that the blood-cerebro-spinal fluid barrier is much more significant in Zn homeostasis in brain.
zinc is not readily available in the brain and that the brain has to actively transport zinc into the brain from the blood.
zinc is not only present in the brain but also it is actively transported into the brain from the blood and cerebrospinal fluid (csf).
